edi_001: You can recognise them by the pair standing evergreen on either side of the entrance. They stand at the courtyard entrance to Craigmillar Castle.
edi_002: You can recognise it by its reduced, cut-back crown, kept alive by recent pruning of its failing branches. It stands on the Pond Lawn, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh.
edi_005: You can recognise them by their rigid, spiralling branches armoured in sharp scale-like leaves, a shape nothing else here shares. They stand near the rose garden at Lauriston Castle.
edi_006: You can recognise them by their weeping habit and glossy, oversized leaves, a pair standing in the King's garden. They stand in the Palace of Holyroodhouse Garden.
edi_009: You can recognise them by their unusual height, clearing 130 feet in the sheltered valley floor. They stand along the Braid Burn, in the Hermitage of Braid.
edi_016: You can recognise it by its ring of trunks around a hollow centre, grown from lower branches that rooted where they touched the ground. It stands in the old grounds of Ormiston Hall.
